clue.text: With a short dagger thrust possibly harm a leading prince

indicators.note: leading places the rearranged letters at the front, ahead of the rest
possibly suggests the letters of the words harm a could be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a jab is a quick stabbing thrust, as with a dagger

explanation.surface: An assassin with a dagger might stab and injure a prince at the head of the procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HARM A to MAHAR, and 'short' trims JAB to JA. 'leading' puts the rearranged letters first. A dagger thrust is a jab.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja is an Indian ruling prince, literally 'great king' in Sanskrit.

clue.text: Bit of a stink, involving everybody, upset religious leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards
involving means one word takes in the other

parts.note: a hum is a bad smell, British slang
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A minor scandal, embroiling everyone, upsets a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts one word inside the other, giving HALLUM; 'upset' turns that around in this down clue. 'Bit of a' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullah is a Muslim cleric learned in Islamic law and theology.

clue.text: Delicate matter of smuggled drug to answer to

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen or illicit goods
pot is slang for cannabis
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sensitive matter involving smuggled narcotics that someone must answer for.
explanation.walkthrough: HOT here means stolen or contraband, as in hot goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a controversial issue that is awkward to deal with.

clue.text: Withdraw soldiers over extended area

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places one piece above the other

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
a tract is a large stretch of land

explanation.surface: Troops are pulled back from a large stretch of territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' stacks the soldiers above the area in this down clue. RE (Royal Engineers) is a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or draw in, so it is a synonym of withdraw.

clue.text: Very pleasurable all-expenses-paid trip

definitions.meaning: a junket at someone else's expense

explanation.surface: A free trip with every cost covered sounds most enjoyable.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly is British slang for very, an adjective meaning merry or pleasant, and a noun for a freebie outing.

clue.text: The party to beat

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a lively party
to beat soundly, as in a fight or a match

explanation.surface: Someone invites a guest to a party where a rival will be given a hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrash is informal slang for a wild party, and also a verb meaning to flog or defeat heavily.

clue.text: Thing cryptically rendering clue?

parts.note: giving a clue obliquely is dropping a suggestion; the word thing, with in, can also be rearranged to give the letters

explanation.surface: A question about what it is that turns something into a puzzle clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinting means suggesting something indirectly, which is what a cryptic clue does.

clue.text: Honour given to a French illustrator

parts.note: Gustave Dore was a famous nineteenth-century French illustrator and engraver

explanation.surface: Recognition is awarded to an artist from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustave Dore illustrated the Bible, Dante and Don Quixote.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore is to worship or revere, so it is a synonym of honour as a verb.

clue.text: Such a talented person making blue movie

definitions.meaning: a person who is extremely good at something
an erotic or pornographic film, as sexy material is called

explanation.surface: A gifted performer is making an adult film.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot stuff is slang for someone highly skilled or attractive, and for sexually explicit material.

clue.text: Lassie possibly in trouble after she upset gym lesson

indicators.note: after places the word for trouble behind the others

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: PE, physical education, is a school gym lesson
to dog is to trouble or plague someone

explanation.surface: Lassie may be in difficulty after a girl ruined the PE class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the gym lesson backwards in this down clue; 'after' puts the trouble word last. Lassie is the famous collie of film and TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie was a rough collie, a breed used for herding, so she is an example.

clue.text: With washing to dry would you be very relaxed?

definitions.text: With washing to dry would you be very relaxed?

parts.words: With washing to dry would you be very relaxed?
parts.note: laundry pegged on a line is literally left dangling; the same phrase is slang for being uninhibited and laid-back

explanation.surface: A question about whether hanging out the laundry is a calming chore.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to behave in a completely uninhibited, relaxed way, and literally describes washing hung on the line.

clue.text: Old man almost involved in some irregularity

indicators.note: involved in means these letters are wrapped within another word

parts.note: some, as in 'some people', means any

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: An elderly man is mixed up in some kind of irregular business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims a letter off the man; with O that goes 'involved in' the word for some, between its N and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is a deviation from the normal rule, an oddity or irregularity.

clue.text: Demanding, politely, man is put on English team

indicators.note: in this across clue, one piece is put on (after) another, so the second named piece comes first

parts.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team
gent is the polite word for a man

explanation.surface: A courteous gentleman is drafted into the England side and proves demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put on' places the polite man after the other pieces. XI (eleven) is the usual crossword team, from cricket and football sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent describes something pressing or requiring much, as in exigent circumstances or exigent demands.

clue.text: Be in sudden rush to get across town

parts.note: to dart is to make a sudden rush
to ford a river is to get across it

explanation.surface: Someone in a hurry dashes across town to arrive somewhere in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be in' and 'to' are just link words. DARTFORD is a town in Kent, south-east England, at the Thames crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartford is a Kent town, so it is an example of the general word in the clue.

clue.text: Individually placed order for royal autobiography?

definitions.meaning: royals refer to themselves as 'one', so their memoir would be written by themselves about themselves

explanation.surface: Someone orders copies of a royal memoir, singly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed order for' is padding linking the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means one at a time, separately; and a monarch saying 'one' would write a book about one by one.

clue.text: After blunder fellow is to be discharged

indicators.note: After places the abbreviation for fellow behind the word for blunder

parts.note: a goof is a silly blunder

explanation.surface: An employee who made a mistake is going to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' means F comes after GOOF. 'Discharged' suggests dismissal, but the sense is a gun or alarm going off.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun or bomb that goes off is fired or discharged; the phrase also means to explode.

clue.text: Where you are forced to react immediately

definitions.text: Where you are forced to react
definitions.meaning: put in a difficult position requiring a quick response

explanation.surface: Describing a situation that demands an instant response.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means put in an awkward position or doing something at once, without delay.

clue.text: Killer dope, like smack, at first fashionable

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
as means like

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of the word

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A murderer high on dope and heroin, in fashion at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' picks S from smack. Dope and smack suggest drugs, but dope is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a person who murders a prominent figure, a hired killer.

clue.text: Cut film that's not feature length, changing ending

indicators.note: changing ending means the final letter is swapped for another, here T becomes N

parts.note: a short is a brief film, shorter than a feature

explanation.surface: A film editor trims a movie so it is shorter than feature length, altering its ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing ending' swaps the last letter of SHORT, its T, for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorn is the past participle of shear, meaning clipped or cut, as hair or fleece.

clue.text: Novelist's writing a novel halfheartedly inside a month?

indicators.note: inside means the pieces are put within another word

parts.note: Nov is the abbreviation for November
taken as written

indicators.note: halfheartedly means one of the two middle letters is removed

parts.note: a novel is a book

explanation.surface: An author writing a book half-heartedly over the course of a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halfheartedly' drops one of the two middle Os of the book; 'inside' places the pieces within the month. Vladimir Nabokov wrote Lolita.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was a Russian-American writer of fiction such as Lolita and Pale Fire.

clue.text: Cake ingredient, say, good with cream

parts.note: e.g., for example, is signalled by say
cream is an off-white colour, so it can stand for white

explanation.surface: A recipe note: one cake ingredient, for instance, goes well with cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives EG (for example). The surface makes you think of a cake topping, but cream stands for a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg white, the albumen, is used in many cakes such as meringues and sponges.

clue.text: In Home Guard, difficulty doctor had over hat

indicators.note: In means the pieces go inside the abbreviation

parts.note: HG is the abbreviation for the Home Guard, Britain's wartime volunteer militia

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means flipped upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'
MO, Medical Officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: In Dad's Army, a medic with a problem had a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RUB and MO together in this down clue, giving OMBUR; 'In' places it inside. The Home Guard was Britain's WW2 volunteer defence force.
explanation.definitionFit: A homburg is a man's felt hat with a dented crown and curled brim.

clue.text: Rig trap up for young animal

parts.note: rig means outfit or equipment, kit

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a net traps animals

explanation.surface: Set up a snare to catch a young creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NET to TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is a young cat, so it is an example of a young animal.

clue.text: What's said to encourage ace cricketer suffering set-back during play

parts.note: A is short for ace, as on playing cards

indicators.note: during means these letters are put inside the next word

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

indicators.note: suffering set-back means the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: Encouragement shouted to a star cricketer who has had a setback during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering set-back' turns the cricketer around to TAB; 'during' puts that inside the play word. 'Ace cricketer' looks like a star player, but ace is just A.
explanation.definitionFit: Attaboy is an interjection of encouragement or approval, a contraction of 'that's the boy'.

clue.text: Pay for handle

definitions.meaning: to deal with or behave towards someone

explanation.surface: Is the price paid for the door handle?
explanation.definitionFit: To treat is to pay for another's food or drink; also to deal with someone in a certain way.

clue.text: Former city's ceremony, one that is recalled

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial display

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so these letters are written backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: An ancient city's grand ceremony is remembered by one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns I and IE together to give EII. POMPEII is the Roman city buried by Vesuvius.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was a Roman city destroyed in AD 79, so it no longer exists as a living city.

clue.text: Father giving half-time rapid talk

indicators.note: half-time means the pair of Ts, read as times, is cut down to one

parts.note: patter is fast glib talk

explanation.surface: A football father giving a quick team talk at the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' halves the double T of PATTER, T standing for time. PATER is Latin and old British public-school slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is old-fashioned British slang for father, from Latin.

clue.text: At sea, tug skipper meant to have old loud-hailer

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Aboard a tugboat, the skipper wants an old megaphone to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges the fifteen letters of TUG SKIPPER MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaking trumpet was a cone-shaped device used before electronics to amplify the voice, as at sea.

clue.text: Local name given to musical turn?

indicators.note: turn means the title is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron

explanation.surface: A local person's name is used in a song-and-dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses the musical, giving ATIVE. 'musical turn' looks like a stage act.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is a person born in a place, a local inhabitant as opposed to a visitor.

clue.text: Book to go to trendy resort

parts.note: right-on means fashionable or politically correct

explanation.surface: Advice to reserve a trip to a fashionable seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside resort on England's south coast; right-on is British slang for trendy or correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a well-known English seaside holiday town, an example of a resort.
